hypothesis: The support allocator improves union and leader-removal outcomes but loses common-five wealth. Exact replay of its actual inventories and close decisions finds 11,5,11 pre-2026 whole-account-only cut dates without a current security-level break. Some intact winners subsequently appreciate; others decline. This motivates separating new-entry warning authority from liquidation authority, not assuming warnings were wrong or increasing an arbitrary exposure cap.
unchanged: Independent features, admission, ranking, individual ratcheting support and exits, actual-filled ownership, material winner additions, reentry confirmation, single/sector limits, pending reductions, cash reserves, engine, costs, T+1, next-open and delayed execution. No new forecasts, securities, date rules or model fits. Old families and contracts retain their meanings.
warning_authority: Run the original RiskState against the complete actual NAV history and exact-universe features, retaining every warning and its recovery clock. Its cap continues to multiply the loss budget available to NEW commitments; zero means no additions, including additions to holdings. A broad warning alone no longer mandates liquidating otherwise intact inventory. Security stops, stale-quote exits and the declared funded-book loss budget can still require immediate protective reductions.
funded_risk: For actual observed units, consider already-latched reductions and full security exits without treating them as fills or spendable cash. Projected held-book risk is sum(projected units * max(current marked close minus the nondecreasing campaign stop, 2% of marked close)). Without the cushion, the loss budget is 10% of actual NAV. If projected risk exceeds the budget, impose a STRICT notional ceiling equal to projected exposure times budget divided by projected risk and proportionally reduce with unchanged executable declaration rounding. Do not apply an ordinary drift band to an actual loss-budget breach. Outstanding protection still blocks all purchases.
cushion: When enabled, keep the maximum of initial capital and every actual observed NAV permanently; never reset it on recovery. Remaining loss room is NAV minus (1-Config.risk_drawdown) times that maximum. Budget is min(10% of NAV, max(1% of NAV, remaining loss room)). The 1% of NAV exploration-risk floor is explicitly part of the candidate, not a guarantee against further losses or a waiver of any drawdown target. Existing warning-driven entry freezes still apply to this floor.
allocation: Use the same parent's loss-distance and cash allocator, but new-commitment risk is the funded-book budget multiplied by the original warning cap. Existing actual units consume that risk first. The independent notional exposure ceiling remains at most one. Do not spend projected sale proceeds or reset the actual NAV curve, campaign stop, global peak or an unresolved protective instruction.
implementation: Introduce two behavior-preserving explicit extension points in support_budget.Owner: _risk_limit(observation,cap) and _exposure_ceiling(cap,cut). Their default behavior must remain byte-for-byte equivalent in decisions to the measured parent on a targeted actual-fill replay. A funded_risk owner supplies the new authority and audited warning state. Preserve current support-budget tests, source-bound archives and the concurrent risk_reliability family.

hard loss-budget reduction without drift allowance
global actual NAV peak never reset

prefix, removal and delayed T+1 invariants

selection: Unchanged finite_study 2025-12-31 cutoff, three core scopes, incumbent wealth/drawdown/fill minimax deficits, existing objective and tie-breaks. Exactly two candidates. No pooling different winners or tuning against 2026.
evaluation: Same selected candidate and unchanged full, bull, late-June-through-August, July-August and retrospective-2026 windows. Original native references, broader pools/removals/subsets, costs, delays and all original economic acceptance obligations remain.
limitation: Support risk is a close-time modeled loss quantity, not a realized-loss guarantee. Gaps, limits, stale quotes, correlated losses and adjusted-unit accounting limitations remain. No failed evidence is promoted or erased.
